text: Lessons 6 through 9 built up the theory — source systems, ETL and ELT, lakes and warehouses, semantic models. Power BI's lineage view is where that theory becomes a screen you can actually click through: a workspace-level diagram showing every data source, semantic model, dataflow, report, and dashboard, connected by the exact lineage relationships between them. Every workspace gets one automatically; nobody has to draw it.

From a workspace's list view, open the View dropdown and select Lineage. You need at least a Contributor role in that workspace, plus a Power BI Pro license, just to see it — Viewers can't switch to this view at all.

The canvas lays out every artifact as a card, left to right, in the direction data actually flows — data sources, then semantic models and dataflows, then reports, then dashboards. Each connecting line is a lineage edge, the exact relationship the last four lessons described in the abstract, now rendered automatically instead of documented by hand. Semantic model and dataflow cards also show their last refresh time, and whether they're certified or promoted — a governance signal Lesson 11 covers in more depth.

A busy workspace can have dozens of cards. Select the double-arrow icon under any one of them, and Power BI highlights everything connected to it, upstream and downstream, and dims everything else. This is the single most useful move in the whole view for anyone doing real lineage work — instead of reading the entire canvas, you isolate just the one thread you actually care about, a one-click preview of the impact-analysis technique Chapter 3 covers in depth.

Select the card itself, instead of the double-arrow icon, and a side panel opens with that artifact's full metadata — sensitivity label, endorsement status, refresh time, and every table it contains, without leaving the canvas. Between the diagram and this panel, lineage view answers both halves of the question: the panel tells you what the artifact is, the diagram tells you what it's connected to.
Next lesson: zooming out from one workspace's lineage view to an enterprise-wide catalog, and what the same chain looks like when it ends at a dashboard an executive checks every morning.
